Helmet detection model card

What the model is, what it was trained on, what it should and should not be used for.

Quick answer

A YOLOv8s object detector with two classes, helmet and no_helmet, fine-tuned on public helmet datasets and on CCTV frames from Myanmar traffic cameras. It is meant to screen road footage for riders without helmets, with a person reviewing each alert.

Model details
NameAxom AI helmet detector, CCTV fine-tune (October 2026)
ArchitectureUltralytics YOLOv8s (about 11.1 million parameters)
TaskObject detection of heads with two classes: helmet (0), no_helmet (1)
InputRGB image; 960 px used for training and 768 px for live CCTV; a 416 px ONNX build runs on phones
Companion modelsCOCO-pretrained YOLOv8s (finds motorcycles); YOLOv8n-cls head-crop classifier (second opinion)
DeveloperAxom AI (Samarjit Kashyap), Guwahati, Assam, India
Code licenceMIT. The weights are derived from Ultralytics YOLOv8 (AGPL-3.0) and datasets under CC BY 4.0 and MIT.
Repositorygithub.com/Samarjitkashyp/helmet-detection

Intended use

  • Screening traffic-camera footage and uploaded videos for motorcycle riders without a helmet, with human review of each alert.
  • Road-safety studies and awareness campaigns.
  • Research and education on object detection and tracking.

Out-of-scope use

  • Automatic fines or penalties without human review.
  • Identifying people. The system does not recognise faces or read plates, and should not be extended to.
  • Safety-critical decisions where a miss or a false alarm could cause harm.
  • Night scenes, heavy rain or very distant riders, until validated on your own footage.

Training data

SourceUsed forLicence
Seven public Roboflow Universe datasets (about 11.7 thousand training images; helmets, riders, caps, hats, hijabs, head accessories)First modelCC BY 4.0, one MIT
HELMET dataset: 910 traffic-camera clips from Myanmar, 100 frames each, 1080pCCTV fine-tune and all CCTV testsCC BY 4.0

Labels for the CCTV fine-tune were derived from the dataset's per-motorcycle ground truth: our detector found heads inside each motorcycle and each head received the bike's label when every person on it agreed. Caps, hats, hijabs and scarves are labelled no_helmet.

Evaluation

SetPrecisionRecallmAP@50
Held-out CCTV frames (500 frames, 1,114 riders)0.7980.7910.748

Live-worker results at one and two analysed frames per second, speed and night tests are on the results page.

Limitations and bias

  • Geography and setting. The CCTV data is from Myanmar. Clothing, helmet styles, road layouts and camera angles differ in other places.
  • Light. Training data is daytime. Night recall is 0.34 on night-style test frames; night training has not been done yet.
  • Size and distance. Heads a few pixels wide are missed.
  • Head coverings. Turbans are not in the training data and may be judged wrongly.
  • Frame rate. Fewer analysed frames per second means fewer riders caught.
  • Helmet quality. The model checks whether a helmet is present, not whether it is certified or fastened correctly.

Ethical considerations

  • Alert photos can show faces. Keep them access-controlled (administrators only here), keep them only as long as needed, and follow local privacy law.
  • False alarms and misses happen. Design the process so that a person checks before anyone is affected.
  • Be open with the public when cameras run AI analysis, where the law or good practice requires it.

How to run it

git clone https://github.com/Samarjitkashyp/helmet-detection
cd helmet-detection/backend
pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m services.cctv_worker --url rtsp://... --name Gate --local

The Android app is at github.com/Samarjitkashyp/helmet-detection-mobile-app; install the published build from helmet-detection.aiaxom.co.in/app.

Version history

  • 26 Oct 2026. CCTV fine-tune: recall on held-out CCTV frames 0.62 → 0.79. Per-rider tracker for low frame rates, crop classifier, size check, speed profile.
  • Earlier. First model: seven public datasets, caps and hats as no helmet.
